item.text:
Using the local prior only for the structured country-year facts. I did not use the client matrix. For 2022, Joko Widodo was President of Indonesia, serving the 2019-2024 term; the constitution gave him broad executive power, but the key hard constraints were the two-term limit, DPR/MPR checks, and impeachment limits. He also publicly shut down third-term talk in March-April 2022.

**Retained source set**
1. [Jokowi, Ma'ruf Amin Inaugurated as President, VP](https://setkab.go.id/en/jokowi-maruf-amin-inaugurated-as-president-vp/) | Publisher: Sekretariat Kabinet Republik Indonesia | Date: 2019-10-20 | Precise fact: Jokowi and Ma'ruf Amin were officially inaugurated for the 2019-2024 presidential term. | Period fit: establishes the office in force during 2022. | Ruler attribution: office/term confirmation, not performance. | Limitations: ceremonial source, no policy detail. | Contrary points: none on the office itself.

2. [Undang-Undang Dasar Negara Republik Indonesia](https://www.pajak.go.id/id/undang-undang-dasar-negara-republik-indonesia) | Publisher: Direktorat Jenderal Pajak / Government of Indonesia | Date: standing constitutional text | Precise fact: the President commands the armed forces, appoints and dismisses ministers, needs DPR approval for laws/treaties in specified cases, cannot dissolve the DPR, and is limited to two terms. | Period fit: the governing constitutional framework in 2022. | Ruler attribution: office-level authority and constraints. | Limitations: legal text, not a behavior record. | Contrary points: political disputes concern interpretation, not the text itself.

3. [President Jokowi on Third Term: We Have to Comply with Constitution](https://setkab.go.id/en/president-jokowi-on-third-term-we-have-to-comply-with-constitution/) | Publisher: Sekretariat Kabinet Republik Indonesia | Date: 2022-03-30 | Precise fact: Jokowi said the constitution clearly regulates presidential terms and “we must comply with and obey the Constitution.” | Period fit: directly addresses the 2022 third-term debate. | Ruler attribution: Jokowi’s own public position. | Limitations: self-statement, not an independent assessment. | Contrary points: does not prove the broader coalition had stopped pushing the idea.

4. [Tamat Isu Perpanjangan Jabatan Presiden](https://news.detik.com/berita/d-6020438/tamat-isu-perpanjangan-jabatan-presiden) | Publisher: detikcom | Date: 2022-04-07 | Precise fact: Jokowi told ministers not to discuss election delay or presidential term extension and framed the issue as over. | Period fit: captures the April 2022 political backlash and reversal. | Ruler attribution: direct evidence of Jokowi’s response to the pressure. | Limitations: news report of a cabinet meeting, not a transcript. | Contrary points: the article reflects reporting on the episode, not a constitutional ruling.

5. [Soal Reshuffle Kabinet, Seskab: Kewenangan Penuh Presiden](https://setkab.go.id/soal-reshuffle-kabinet-seskab-kewenangan-penuh-presiden/) | Publisher: Sekretariat Kabinet Republik Indonesia | Date: 2022-06-14 | Precise fact: cabinet reshuffles are described as fully within the President’s prerogative. | Period fit: documents a live 2022 exercise of executive authority. | Ruler attribution: shows real presidential control over the cabinet. | Limitations: a spokesperson’s framing, not a legal text. | Contrary points: no contrary factual claim on the prerogative itself.

6. [Indonesia passes law to relocate capital to Borneo jungle](https://uk.investing.com/news/economy/indonesia-passes-law-to-relocate-capital-to-remote-borneo-2563833) | Publisher: Reuters | Date: 2022-01-18 | Precise fact: parliament approved the IKN law, creating the legal basis for Jokowi’s capital relocation project. | Period fit: major early-2022 inherited policy project. | Ruler attribution: long-horizon agenda set by Jokowi’s administration, not personal credit alone. | Limitations: event-level reporting, not implementation outcomes. | Contrary points: the article itself notes it was a long-running idea, not uniquely Jokowi’s invention.

7. [Jokowi to appoint authority head and deputy head of Nusantara city](https://en.antaranews.com/news/216253/jokowi-to-appoint-authority-head-and-deputy-head-of-nusantara-city) | Publisher: ANTARA News | Date: 2022-02-20 | Precise fact: the IKN law gave Jokowi power to appoint, consult on, and dismiss the Nusantara authority head and deputy head. | Period fit: confirms concrete executive authority in 2022. | Ruler attribution: directly attributable to the president’s office. | Limitations: state wire reporting on the law, not on whether the project succeeded. | Contrary points: not evidence of implementation quality.

8. [State of the Nation Address of the President of the Republic of Indonesia at the Annual Session of the MPR, DPR and DPD, 2022](https://setkab.go.id/state-of-the-nation-address-of-the-president-of-the-republic-of-indonesia-at-the-annual-session-of-the-peoples-consultative-assembly-mpr-of-the-republic-of-indonesia-and-the-joint-session-o/) | Publisher: Sekretariat Kabinet Republik Indonesia | Date: 2022-08-16 | Precise fact: Jokowi said the government was still pursuing past gross human rights violations, continued follow-up to Komnas HAM findings, and he had signed the nonjudicial settlement decree. | Period fit: the main annual policy statement for 2022. | Ruler attribution: direct presidential policy statement. | Limitations: self-justifying state address, not an adjudication. | Contrary points: civil society disputed the nonjudicial approach.

9. [Jokowi Diminta Batalkan Keppres soal Pelanggaran HAM Berat](https://news.detik.com/berita/d-6239669/jokowi-diminta-batalkan-keppres-soal-pelanggaran-ham-berat) | Publisher: detikcom | Date: 2022-08-17 | Precise fact: civil society groups argued the decree would protect impunity and should be cancelled. | Period fit: immediate critical reaction to the August 2022 decree. | Ruler attribution: shows political and civil-society pushback on Jokowi’s decision. | Limitations: advocacy framing, not neutral adjudication. | Contrary points: the government defended the decree as victim-centered.

10. [Protests across Indonesia as anger mounts over fuel price increase](https://www.euronews.com/2022/09/04/indonesia-subsidies) | Publisher: Reuters | Date: 2022-09-04 | Precise fact: Jokowi raised subsidized fuel prices by about 30% to control a ballooning subsidy budget, triggering protests. | Period fit: one of the biggest domestic political-economic events of 2022. | Ruler attribution: directly tied to Jokowi’s policy choice. | Limitations: Reuters focused on the macro decision, not local distributional effects. | Contrary points: government argued the subsidy burden made the hike unavoidable.

11. [Indonesian murder trial puts spotlight on police impunity](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/indonesian-murder-trial-puts-spotlight-on-police-impunity-2913292) | Publisher: Reuters | Date: 2022-10-17 | Precise fact: the Sambo murder trial spotlighted alleged impunity and corruption in the police force. | Period fit: useful for the 2022 rule-of-law/institutional context. | Ruler attribution: institutional context, not a personal misconduct allegation against Jokowi. | Limitations: not a direct presidential action story. | Contrary points: it does not prove Jokowi directed the conduct described.

12. [President Jokowi Opens G20 Summit](https://setkab.go.id/en/president-jokowi-opens-g20-summit/) | Publisher: Sekretariat Kabinet Republik Indonesia | Date: 2022-11-15 | Precise fact: Jokowi formally opened the G20 Summit in Bali and said Indonesia was honored to host the presidency. | Period fit: the year’s biggest foreign-policy stage. | Ruler attribution: direct presidential diplomacy and state capacity signal. | Limitations: ceremonial and summit-opening language, not an outcome measure. | Contrary points: success at hosting does not settle domestic governance questions.

**Compact event map**
- January-February: IKN law passed; Jokowi gets a major long-horizon development project and direct appointment power over the capital authority.
- March-April: third-term and election-delay speculation peaks; Jokowi publicly rejects it and orders ministers to stop talking about it.
- June: cabinet reshuffle occurs, reinforcing the President’s prerogative over the executive team.
- August: annual state address pairs a human-rights decree with broader development claims; civil society immediately attacks the nonjudicial approach.
- September: fuel subsidy cuts and price increases trigger nationwide protests.
- October: police-impunity scandal keeps rule-of-law weakness in the foreground.
- November: Jokowi hosts and opens the G20 in Bali, a major foreign-policy and state-capacity event.

**Chapter source plan**
- 1B: no ruler-specific narrative source is needed yet; if revisited, use FAS, NTI, SIPRI, and official defense statements.
- 2B: keep the local UCDP/SIPRI priors; add only narrative follow-up from Reuters or official defense statements if attribution becomes necessary.
- 3B: use detik, Reuters, and human-rights/civil-society reactions around the August decree and protest episodes.
- 4B: use the constitution, Setkab, detik protest coverage, and Reuters for term-limit, rights, press, and protest constraints.
- 5B: use macroeconomic official sources and Reuters on fuel/inflation pressure; the local priors already cover the quantitative base.
- 6B: use WHO, UNDP, and official health/education sources; narrative only if you need policy attribution.
- 7B: use KPK, Reuters, detik investigative/reporting, and the rights-decree controversy for corruption and accountability context.
- 8B: use the local governance priors plus official planning documents, Reuters, and state-secrectariat material for implementation capacity and executive effectiveness.
